- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to peak too high immediately after a price spike, then gradually decline — but often overshoot the true mean reversion path.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days of the forecast, then underestimates later days.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured — model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price behavior suggests.
- Forecasts show a lagged response to recent price drops — model takes longer to adjust downward than the true price does.
- When the true price drops sharply, model often fails to recognize the magnitude of the drop and underestimates the decline.
- Model tends to overfit recent volatility, leading to overreaction to short-term noise rather than long-term trends.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 5–15% for the first 10 days if the prior 30-day average was above 70.00.
- If the model forecast exceeds the 30-day moving average by more than 10%, reduce it by 5–10% for the next 5 days.
- When true price falls below 68.00, model should reduce forecast by 3–5% per day until price stabilizes.
